author: Han Li
description:
A US House committee on Thursday released confidential licence applications from Chinese companies seeking to buy advanced artificial intelligence chips from Nvidia and AMD, information normally protected under US export-control law.
Brian Mast, a Florida Republican and chair of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, used his authority under the Export Control Reform Act to make public the details of Nvidia and AMD licence applications to sell AI chips to China.
“[The Committee] determines that...
title: US Congress releases list of Chinese firms seeking Nvidia chips

author: Lucy Quaggin
description:
The United States sanctioned three individuals and two companies on Thursday over their alleged links to scam centre compounds in Southeast Asia, in the latest US crackdown on networks connected to Chinese-born tycoon Chen Zhi.
“Southeast Asia-based scam centres, most of them run by Chinese organised crime groups, stole an estimated US$18.2 billion from Americans in 2025,” said US State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott. “These criminal enterprises steal billions of dollars from victims around...
title: US crackdown on scam networks connected to Chinese-born tycoon Chen Zhi ramps up

author: Nayan Seth
description:
The seating arrangement at Thursday’s historic trilateral summit in Shenzhen sparked debate among former US officials and analysts over whether the optics reflected standard host protocol or a deliberate bid by China to place itself at the centre of the discussions.
“A stunning image of a China-centred order: a would-be G3 with Xi presiding,” said Julian Gewirtz, who served as senior director for China and Taiwan affairs at the White House National Security Council during the Joe Biden...
title: China-centred order or host duties? Experts weigh in on Xi-Trump-Putin seating

author: Mark Magnier
description:
What was teased for weeks as an unprecedented three-way photo opportunity ended up rattling the geopolitical landscape on Thursday with the release of a China-US-Russia joint “peace declaration” outlining areas of cooperation in worldwide energy markets, nuclear non-proliferation and global governance.
At the conclusion of the first-ever three-way meeting in Shenzhen between Chinese President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin, the trio issued a statement...
title: Xi, Trump and Putin ‘peace declaration’ suggests summit is more than a photo op

author: Reuters
description:
The US ⁠Federal Communications Commission voted on Thursday ⁠to ban Chinese telecoms firms from direct access to US phone numbers on national security grounds – a measure designed to prevent scam-related robocalls.
The action will bar China Mobile, China Telecom and China Unicom and other IP-enabled service providers from ‌direct access. The FCC previously barred the three firms from providing international telecommunications services to the US.
For telecoms firms providing Voice over Internet...
title: FCC votes to ban Chinese telecoms from direct access to US phone numbers

author: Fan Chen
description:
Thursday’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit in Shenzhen saw unprecedented three-way talks between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin as well as separate bilateral meetings between the presidents.
Here are some of the key events from this important day of China diplomacy.
Nuclear pledge
In a peace declaration after the three-way summit, the three heads of state reaffirmed that a nuclear war “cannot be won and must never be fought”.
They also pledged to hold further talks...
title: Nuclear arms, energy supplies - but no Kim: the main takeaways from a historic Apec summit

author: Josephine Ma,Amber Wang
description:
When the leaders of the world’s three biggest nuclear powers sat down for talks in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen on Thursday, they not only made history, they were likely setting a precedent.
The presidents of China, Russia and the United States – countries that were once also wartime allies – came together for the first time for a summit on the sidelines of the Apec leaders’ meeting.
Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump spent 90 minutes in discussion around a circular table at...
title: China, Russia and the US: 3 presidents, 3 nuclear powers and 1 historic precedent

author: SCMP
description:
We have put together the top ten stories from our coverage of the 2026 Apec summit held in Shenzhen, China. If you would like to see more of our reporting, please consider subscribing.
1. Handshakes, hugs and subtle power plays: decoding the Xi-Trump-Putin dynamic in Shenzhen
After weeks of intense speculation, this year’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit in Shenzhen delivered an unscripted diplomatic spectacle – where every lingering handshake, pat on the back and side-by-side...
title: Power plays, verbal displays, Xi-Trump-Putin talk: historic Apec summit explained

author: Khushboo Razdan,Alyssa Chen,Dewey Sim
description:
When the leaders of China, the United States and Russia sat down in Shenzhen, the rest of Asia watched with a mix of cautious optimism and wary anticipation – knowing that any deal struck behind closed doors might redraw the regional balance of power.
The historic meeting between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin marked the first-ever three-way talks between the leaders of the world’s major nuclear powers, and another such meeting is a possibility next month when the US hosts the Group...
title: Asia watches from the outside waiting to see if Xi-Trump-Putin talks bear fruit

author: Cao Jiaxuan
description:
After weeks of intense speculation, this year’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit in Shenzhen delivered an unscripted diplomatic spectacle – where every lingering handshake, pat on the back and side-by-side stride carried as much weight as the closed-door talks.
The tone was set before the leaders’ summit even officially began. Breaking with decades of protocol, Chinese President Xi Jinping personally appeared on the tarmac at Shenzhen Baoan International Airport to greet US...
title: Handshakes, hugs and subtle power plays: decoding the Xi-Trump-Putin dynamic in Shenzhen

author: Alyssa Chen
description:
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi thanked Chinese President Xi Jinping for inviting her to the Apec summit and congratulated him on successfully hosting the event on Thursday.
Speaking at a press conference at the end of her visit to Shenzhen, Takaichi described her brief interactions with the Chinese leader.
Unlike other leaders, she did not have a one-on-one meeting with Xi, but after a quick handshake at Wednesday’s welcome banquet, she spoke to him for around 10 seconds on Thursday...
title: Japanese PM Takaichi tries to break ice with Xi by thanking him for hosting Apec summit

author: Eve Qiao
description:
When Vietnam’s first lady Ngo Phuong Ly shook hands with China’s Peng Liyuan in the receiving line at Wednesday night’s Apec welcome banquet in Shenzhen, Peng seemed impressed by her guest’s outfit.
After posing for photographs, the two appeared to exchange a few words about the outfit, a traditional black-and-silver ao dai – a long, side-slit tunic worn over trousers – adorned with white cranes.
Ly was not the only guest to use the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen to...
title: Apec sartorial diplomacy: first ladies Peng Liyuan, Ngo Phuong Ly and Kim Hea-kyung shine

author: Fan Chen
description:
Two Latin American presidents have shown their appreciation for tech advancements in musical instruments on display during the Apec summit in Shenzhen.
Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum was captured playing a traditional Chinese folk song, “Jasmine Flower”, using a stringless guitar ahead of the welcome banquet on Wednesday evening.


Sheinbaum praised China’s emerging technology in an interview with local Chinese media.
“From what I have been seeing, there is a great deal of high technology –...
title: Presidents of Mexico, Peru enchanted by Chinese tech advances in musical instruments

author: Brian Rhoads,Neil Denslow
description:
President Xi Jinping highlighted the “pioneering significance” of the first trilateral meeting between the leaders of China, the United States and Russia, as Donald Trump pushed for talks on nuclear weapons.
“When major countries live in harmony, the world enjoys peace,” Xi said at the start of the meeting in Shenzhen. “When major countries clash, the world falls into chaos.”
Trump said that the three nations are “uniquely positioned to discuss how to reduce the number of nuclear weapons on...
title: Xi-Trump-Putin trilateral breaks historic ground

author: William Zheng
description:
In high-stakes summitry, seating charts and delegation rosters often speak louder than boilerplate communiques.
And, as the unprecedented China-US-Russia trilateral meeting unfolds in Shenzhen, the strategic agendas of the three powers can be discerned by the security and economic tsars, top diplomatic strategists and influential technocrats flanking the three leaders.
Chinese President Xi Jinping and his counterparts Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin met on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific...
title: Who’s who in Shenzhen: the priorities revealed by Xi-Trump-Putin summit rosters

author: Phoebe Zhang
description:
Shenzhen residents may have been kept at a distance from the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit their city hosted, but some had the opportunity to encounter dignitaries who made time to explore the Chinese metropolis.
Social media users posted on Wednesday that they saw Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast at a shop for Pagoda, a leading Chinese fruit chain retailer, discussing business deals with local fruit importers.
Pagoda opened its first store in 2002 and has risen to become...
title: While locals lie low, visiting Apec leaders explore Shenzhen’s streets and shops

author: Albee Zhang
description:
All three US presidential Boeing 747s touched down in Manila earlier this week, the first stop on Donald Trump’s Asia tour.
The US Air Force typically deploys a backup aircraft on major overseas trips, but seeing the entire fleet at a single foreign airport was an unusual sight.
The jumbo jets are best known for flying as Air Force One, the call sign used by any US Air Force aircraft carrying the sitting president.
The fleet includes two older Boeing 747-200s, designated VC-25As, that entered...
title: Qatar-gifted Boeing 747 makes China debut as Air Force One in Shenzhen

author: Amber Wang
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin began a historic trilateral meeting on Thursday afternoon, marking the first-ever three-way summit between the leaders of the world’s major nuclear powers.
The meeting is taking place in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit. If Putin travels to Miami for the Group of 20 (G20) summit next month, the three could have a second...
title: Xi invokes WWII alliance, Trump raises nuclear cuts in 3-way talks with Putin

author: Fan Chen
description:
The choice of a classic Philippine song about remorse and forgiveness to welcome President Ferdinand Marcos Jnr to the Apec state gala has sparked widespread debate online about whether it was sending a subtle message about the country’s disputes with China.
A Chinese orchestra played the song “Anak”, which means child, when Marcos entered the hall in Shenzhen before greeting Chinese President Xi Jinping and first lady Peng Liyuan and posing for a photo with the other leaders.
The song, written...
title: Was China’s choice of welcome song for Philippine leader sending a subtle message?

author: Xinyi Wu
description:
Danny Quah is an economics professor at the National University of Singapore’s Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy. He served as the school’s dean between 2018 and 2025, and has consulted for, among others, the World Bank, the Bank of England and the Monetary Authority of Singapore.
Here, he discusses how the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) navigates the US-China rivalry, yuan internationalisation in the region and why the “China shock” has played out differently in Southeast...
title: Danny Quah on Asean’s middle course and a prisoner’s dilemma for US, China

author: Eve Qiao
description:
Vietnamese leader To Lam and his wife, Ngo Phuong Ly, had just moved on. Russian President Vladimir Putin had yet to appear. In the lull, Peng Liyuan took a step towards her husband, Chinese President Xi Jinping.
She began to speak, pointing ahead and to her right as Xi’s gaze followed her gesture before returning to her. They stood close while they talked in the brief interval – no more than a minute and a half – before the next guest arrived.
As China’s first couple welcomed Asia-Pacific...
title: Side by side in Shenzhen: inside Xi Jinping and Peng Liyuan’s first-couple diplomacy

author: Laura Zhou
description:
During a high-profile trip to the southern tech hub of Shenzhen, Elon Musk said his young son loved China because the country “makes almost everything” – including his toys.
In a short video released on Thursday, the SpaceX and Tesla chief executive described himself as a “huge fan” of both China and its technology in a meeting with Ren Hongbin, chairman of the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade.
Musk then turned to his six-year-old son, X Æ A-Xii, who was seated beside...
title: ‘Toy paradise’: Elon Musk says his 6-year-old son loves China

author: Cao Jiaxuan
description:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio was once again generous in his admiration for China’s grand architecture, this time at the Apec summit’s welcome dinner ahead of Thursday’s main meeting.
At the Shenzhen International Communication Centre on Wednesday night, Chinese President Xi Jinping and first lady Peng Liyuan welcomed US President Donald Trump and other leaders to the southern tech hub.
A video showed Rubio speaking to China’s ambassador to the United States, Xie Feng, and US ambassador to...
title: Apec summit finds Marco Rubio again admiring Chinese architecture

author: Shi Huang
description:
In Chongzuo, Guangxi, at the southernmost tip of China, steep limestone peaks rise abruptly, disappearing into the humid and dense tropical rainforest.
For tens of thousands of years, this green labyrinth of interwoven vegetation has not only swallowed sunlight and footprints but also preserved the secrets of ancient humans.
In Baxian Cave and Naxian Cave on the west bank of the Zuojiang River, archaeologists identified nine tiny ancient human teeth among more than 18,000 mammalian...
title: Homo erectus teeth found in China’s rainforest topple theory of human evolution

author: Dewey Sim
description:
US President Donald Trump says he will press China on agricultural purchases as talks begin with his counterpart Xi Jinping on Thursday.
The request on the sidelines of the Apec summit in Shenzhen comes as Trump stresses that the two leaders have made their relationship “fair”.
In his opening remarks of their meeting, Trump said he would ask Xi to “do some more for our farmers”, citing China’s “insatiable appetite”. He also cited the Ukraine war, energy security and Iran in his comments.


He...
title: As talks with Xi get under way, Trump asks China to do more for US farmers

author: Phoebe Zhang,Carol Yang
description:
As world leaders start a new day of talks at the Apec summit in Shenzhen, US President Donald Trump was seen seemingly dozing off in his seat.
While President Xi Jinping was outlining China’s hopes for the Asia-Pacific, the 80-year-old apparently nodded off, live feed showed. Meanwhile, Russian President Vladimir Putin’s gaze remained fixed on the proceedings, and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Hong Kong’s leader John Lee took notes.
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi was seen...
title: After days of travel and diplomacy, Trump seems to nod off during Apec speeches

author: Amber Wang
description:
When Chinese President Xi Jinping broke decades of diplomatic precedent to greet US President Donald Trump on the tarmac in Shenzhen on Wednesday, cameras caught a woman in a striking yellow dress standing a few steps from the two leaders.
That ever-present figure is Monica Crowley, the 35th chief of protocol of the United States.

In high-stakes summitry, she is an invisible stage manager responsible for the diplomatic logistics and ceremonial choreography of the US president’s foreign...
title: Meet Monica Crowley, the US protocol chief orchestrating Trump’s Apec optics

author: Carol Yang
description:
Apec leaders were given Chinese-style scarves to wear for the group summit photo on Thursday.
It was a pared-back nod to the forum’s tradition of dressing attendees in the host economy’s sartorial heritage.
The scarves came in two colours: red and blue. Most leaders, including Chinese President Xi Jinping, opted for red, while US President Donald Trump and his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin wore blue.
The hem of each scarf is embroidered with the summit emblem, which features 21 intertwined...
title: Apec leaders suit up with a scarf for a family photo in Shenzhen

author: Alyssa Chen
description:
Under the neon glow of the Shenzhen skyline on Wednesday evening, US President Donald Trump offered onlookers an unexpected view of himself.
As his armoured presidential limousine – known as “The Beast” – glided down Shenzhen’s avenues en route to the Apec welcome dinner, Trump was clearly visible as he looked through the thick glass to view the southern tech hub’s nightscape.

Video footage circulating online showed Trump gazing at the skyscrapers and raising his fist towards the delighted...
title: Chinese onlookers get a new view of Trump as he takes in the view of Shenzhen

author: Phoebe Zhang
description:
When Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi arrived at the Shenzhen International Communication Centre for a welcome banquet for the Apec leaders on Wednesday night, an ensemble on the stage switched to a bittersweet tune.
The music arranged to welcome Takaichi was the Japanese hit “Ue o muite arukou”, known as the Sukiyaki song in the West. It was first released in Japan in 1961 and performed by the late singer Kyu Sakamoto.
The lyrics tell the story of someone who looks up while walking alone,...
title: ‘I look up when I walk’: 1961 hit Sukiyaki welcomes Japan’s Takaichi at Apec gala

author: Liu Zhen
description:
The United States conducted an intercontinental ballistic missile test less than two hours before President Donald Trump landed in China on Wednesday for the Apec summit and a high-stakes trilateral meeting with his Chinese and Russian counterparts.
According to a statement from the US Air Force Global Strike Command, an unarmed Minuteman III missile was launched at 11.01pm Pacific Time on Tuesday from Vandenberg Space Force Base, California, in a test designated Glory Trip 257.


The launch...
title: US launched unarmed ICBM test hours before Trump’s Air Force One landed in China

author: Khushboo Razdan
description:
US President Donald Trump has described China and Russia as “natural enemies” whose partnership “should never have been allowed to happen”, while defending former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang as an irreplaceable genius.
He was speaking in a Fox News interview given just before a bilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and a trilateral with Xi and Russian leader Vladimir Putin.
Trump said China and Russia were driven together by competing needs rather than affinity. “They have 1.4 billion...
title: ‘Natural enemies’: Trump on China-Russia ties as he plays down Nvidia ‘tragedy’

author: SCMP
description:
We have put together stories from our coverage of the first day of Apec in Shenzhen. If you would like to see more of our reporting, please consider subscribing.
1. Rare hug and roaring flyover set stage for historic firsts at Apec in Shenzhen

It was a day of firsts in Shenzhen on Wednesday when Chinese President Xi Jinping personally greeted his American counterpart Donald Trump at the city airport, setting up a historic start to the Apec summit.
2. China’s first lady Peng Liyuan lets her...
title: Peng’s English and Cantonese classics: the Shenzhen Apec details you may have missed

author: SCMP Reporters
description:
This live article is freely available to our registered users. Please log in or create an account.
World leaders are gathering in Shenzhen on Thursday for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) plenary, looking for ways to promote trade and investment at a time of rising global uncertainty.
Chinese President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese are among the leaders...
title: ‘Sailing in same boat’: Xi calls for stronger shared interests in Apec opening remarks

author: Ronny Tong
description:
If you ask what constitutes treason, most people would probably answer: treason is assisting an enemy to harm one’s country. If national security laws existed at the time, historical figures like Qin Hui, Wu Sangui and even Wang Jingwei might all have been found guilty of treason. If you further ask whether treason applies only during times of war, the question becomes somewhat complicated.
Logically and as a matter of principle, treason is an act of betraying one’s country; the emphasis is on...
title: Treason or not, betraying one’s country won’t be tolerated

author: Zhang Tong
description:
Peking University professor Li Yulong’s team celebrated when six scientists detailing their research on detecting neural signals were accepted for the Society for Neuroscience’s 56th annual meeting in Washington – but only four obtained US visas to participate in it.
Li has been regularly attending the world’s largest neuroscience gathering since he was a student in 2000. He described it as an essential forum for sharing findings with researchers worldwide, but said his team’s visa difficulties...
title: US-China science ties fray as visa hurdles and security scrutiny grow

author: Liu Zhen
description:
World leaders have descended on the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen for the Apec summit, and two of them likely brought their “nuclear button” with them.
The United States president’s famous briefcase – nicknamed the “nuclear football” – has yet to be sighted in the Chinese city. The so-called emergency satchel is actually a bulky black briefcase containing war plans and it can be used to send nuclear orders to the Pentagon.
But the Russian equivalent, known as the Cheget, made an unexpected...
title: Apec brings world leaders and probably 2 ‘nuclear briefcases’ to Shenzhen

author: Teresa Elena Frontado,Igor Patrick
description:
A bipartisan US congressional commission has urged lawmakers to declare China’s detention of hundreds of Panama-flagged ships a form of “economic coercion” and to let the US president respond with sanctions, nearly 10 months after Panama’s Supreme Court stripped a subsidiary of Hong Kong-based CK Hutchison Holdings of its right to run two ports on the Panama Canal.
In its annual report to Congress, released on Wednesday, the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission said Beijing had made...
title: US panel urges Congress to punish China over Panama-flagged ship detentions

author: Fan Chen
description:
South Korean first lady Kim Hea Kyung has charmed Chinese social media users with her warmth towards ground staff, personal style and affection for her husband – fuelling online “shipping” of Seoul’s first couple.
Accompanying South Korean President Lee Jae Myung, Kim arrived in Shenzhen early on Wednesday for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit.
Like other visiting dignitaries, Lee and Kim received a red-carpet welcome with an honour guard. More than 100 dancers dressed in white...
title: South Korean first lady Kim Hea Kyung’s warmth and style captivate Chinese social media
